system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Bottom line

The Seller's cover email calls this a "fair and balanced package". It is not. The Seller Update describes several issues as "addressed", "adequate", "settled" or "not material". The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts those descriptions in at least six places: Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006 and the Sandbar renewals. The limitation package would also shift almost all residual risk onto Wattlebridge, including title risk. We should treat the Seller Update as advocacy and work from the Disclosure Letter facts and our own due diligence.

**Caveat:** I have only seen the Seller Update and the Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA text or the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012). The points below should be checked against those before our mark-up goes out.

---

## Part A: Limitation and risk-allocation regime

### 1. Default rule that limitations apply to all Claims (cl 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)
**Issue:** The Seller wants caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to apply to "all Claims of any nature" unless expressly carved out. That default would quietly capture:
- title and capacity claims
- tax claims
- specific indemnities
- leakage and price-adjustment claims
- fraud

**Why it matters:** Any carve-out we forget to draft would be lost. Limiting liability for fraud is also not acceptable, and is unlikely to be effective in any event. Non-reliance and exclusive-remedy wording will be cited against any misleading or deceptive conduct claim under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law. That claim cannot be excluded by contract, but these clauses weaken it in practice.

**Push back:**
- Reverse the default. Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- Expressly exclude the following from all limitations: fraud, wilful concealment or dishonesty; Fundamental Warranties; the tax indemnity; specific indemnities; leakage; and price adjustments.
- Limit non-reliance so it does not cover the Warranties, the Disclosure Letter or fraud.

### 2. Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties capped like general warranties
**Issue:** Title would be capped at AUD 4.8m (20%), subject to the AUD 250k basket and lost after 18 months.

**Why it matters:** Title is the thing we are paying AUD 24m for. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept that. Market practice is a 100% price cap, no thresholds, and a long time limit (typically 5–7 years, or the statutory limitation period).

**Push back:**
- Fundamental Warranties capped at 100% of the price.
- No de minimis or basket.
- Time limit of at least 6 years.

### 3. Cap, thresholds and time limits for general warranties (cl 12.1–12.3)
| Item | Seller | Comment | Buyer counter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Within market range | Open at 30–50%. Consider W&I insurance as a trade |
| De minimis | AUD 25k | About 0.1% of price, at the high end | AUD 10–15k. Related claims aggregate |
| Basket | AUD 250k, excess only | About 1.04% of price, above the usual 0.5–1% range. "Excess only" is Seller-friendly | About AUD 120k, "tipping" (recover from the first dollar once exceeded) |
| Time limit | 18 months | Usually not enough to cover two audit cycles | 24 months general |

### 4. General disclosure of the entire data room and public records (DL 1.1–1.2, Sched 7)
**Issue:** Every fact anywhere in the data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and any "publicly searchable corporate records" would qualify every warranty. The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026.

**Why it matters:** This guts the warranties. It is particularly unfair here because the Disclosure Letter openly says several key facts are unresolved. There is also a six-week gap since the cut-off with no update.

**Push back:**
- Only specific disclosures in the Disclosure Letter qualify the warranties.
- Each disclosure must be fair: enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, made against a specific warranty.
- At most, accept deemed disclosure of identified searches made on stated dates.
- Require an updated or supplementary Disclosure Letter at signing.
- Make clear that any Completion bring-down disclosure does not reduce our remedies.

### 5. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)
**Issue:** This is an anti-sandbagging clause that extends to constructive knowledge ("discoverable") and to our advisers' knowledge.

**Why it matters:** Combined with general disclosure, this effectively converts the warranties into a "buyer beware" sale. Our DD work would become evidence against us.

**Push back:**
- Delete the clause, or have a pro-sandbagging clause: warranties are not affected by Buyer investigation or knowledge.
- Fallback: limit it to actual knowledge of a named Buyer deal team, of the specific breach, excluding advisers and imputed knowledge.

### 6. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
**Issue:** No separate tax indemnity or deed. IP warranties sit under the general cap and time limits.

**Push back:**
- Tax: a separate tax indemnity or deed for pre-Completion tax, dollar-for-dollar, outside the basket and de minimis. Cap at 100% of price. Time limit aligned with ATO amendment periods plus a buffer, typically about 5–7 years.
- IP: given the Ironquay issue (below), core IP ownership warranties should be treated as quasi-fundamental, or covered by a specific indemnity.

---

## Part B: Specific issues where the Seller Update conflicts with its own Disclosure Letter

### 7. Bluefen change-of-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3): high priority
**The conflict:** The Seller Update says consent is "addressed". DL 2 says no final written consent has been provided and there is no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue.

**Why it matters:**
- "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation.
- Treating the condition as satisfied on delivery of a consent letter ignores the clause 11.3 conditions. A conditional or qualified consent could leave the change-of-control right alive.
- Losing 30% of revenue would fundamentally change the valuation.

**Push back:**
- Make this a Condition Precedent that only the Buyer can waive.
- It is satisfied only by an unconditional written consent (or waiver), in a form the Buyer reasonably approves, together with evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are met or permanently waived.
- Seller to use best or all reasonable endeavours.
- Buyer walk-right at the sunset date.
- If the Buyer chooses to waive, fallback options: specific indemnity, price retention or escrow, or an earn-out linked to Bluefen revenue.

### 8. Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m) (cl 2 / 7): high priority
**The conflict:** The Seller Update proposes a release "following Completion". DL 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid, no discharge is in hand, and there is a change-of-control clause (8.1).

**Why it matters:**
- A post-Completion release is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal.
- Completion itself may trigger a change-of-control default or acceleration under clause 8.1.
- The Company's assets, and possibly the Sale Shares, would remain encumbered after Completion.

**Push back:**
- Delivery at Completion of a payoff letter from Riverlark confirming the exact payout figure.
- Deed of release and discharge of all security, including PPSR financing statements (and any share mortgage), effective on receipt of payment.
- Payout made directly from the price through the funds flow and treated as Debt.
- Riverlark waiver or consent for clause 8.1 for any gap period.

### 9. Completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs (funds flow)
**The conflict:** The Seller Update says the funds flow "reflects agreed price mechanics" but the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller". DL 5 confirms the bonuses are not in the funds flow, and is silent on on-costs.

**Why it matters:**
- These are Company obligations triggered by the transaction. If they are not deducted, the Company (and so Wattlebridge) bears them after Completion.
- On-costs could add materially to the AUD 420k: NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee (currently 12%), PAYG withholding obligations, and workers' compensation.

**Push back:**
- Treat bonuses and all on-costs as Transaction Costs / Debt-like items, deducted from the price.
- Pay them through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded from the deduction.
- Uncapped specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- Require a corrected funds flow.
- Separately, check whether the continued-employment conditions affect retention of key staff.

### 10. Ironquay SOW3 IP (cl 11.1)
**The conflict:** The Seller Update says the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate". DL 4 states:
- Under DD-004 clause 7.3, Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
- AUD 180k appears open (unverified).
- There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment.

**Why it matters:** The Company may not own the SOW3 IP. An indemnity limited to the payment amount does not cover the real exposure, which includes:
- loss of ownership of the IP
- infringement claims by Ironquay or third parties
- remediation or re-development costs
- customer impact if the materials are embedded in products

**Push back:**
- Before Completion: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees (with bank verification), plus an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. Make this a Condition Precedent, or at least a Completion deliverable.
- Broaden the indemnity to all Losses arising from the Company not owning, or not having unencumbered rights to, the SOW3 materials.
- The indemnity should sit outside the cap and thresholds, with an appropriate time limit.
- Our IP team should confirm how deeply the SOW3 materials are embedded in the products.

### 11. DD-006 data export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sched 6)
**The conflict:** The Seller Update says it is "not expected to be material". DL 6 says:
- the scope is unknown
- access by an unauthorised person is unknown
- whether notification is required is unknown
- the investigation is preliminary
- about 1,240 records containing personal information may be affected

**Why it matters:**
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach, reasonably and expeditiously, generally within 30 days. If the incident predates 22 September, that window has probably already passed. That creates a compliance exposure in its own right.
- Other potential exposure: regulatory action and penalties under the strengthened Privacy Act regime, OAIC investigation, customer contractual notification obligations, and reputational harm.

**Push back:**
- Before signing or Completion, require the investigation report and the NDB assessment and its outcome.
- Require evidence of any notifications made to the OAIC, affected individuals and customers.
- Pre-Completion covenant to complete the investigation and remediation, with Buyer consultation rights.
- Uncapped (or separately capped) specific indemnity for all Losses from the incident, outside the thresholds.
- Remove the "not material" description from the SPA.

### 12. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330k aggregate)
**The conflict:** The Seller Update says these are "ordinary-course". DL 8 says they should be "read together for timing/scope" and does not state whether they are ordinary course, terminable, accrued or unavoidable.

**Why it matters:** One related commitment split into three AUD 110k pieces suggests contract-splitting. It could be an attempt to stay under a conduct-of-business consent threshold or a materiality threshold. We need to check the SPA thresholds. These may also be commitments the Seller entered into close to the sale that we would not have approved.

**Push back:**
- Obtain the contracts (DD-008, DD-011).
- Confirm the termination rights and how much is accrued or prepaid.
- Aggregate related contracts for any interim-period consent threshold.
- Depending on the findings: Seller-procured termination before Completion; treatment of unaccrued committed amounts as Debt or leakage; or a specific indemnity.

### 13. Title evidenced only by the DD-012 share register
**Issue:** A register maintained by the Company itself is not proof of unencumbered title. DL 10 acknowledges we have not verified it.

**Push back:**
- Run ASIC and PPSR searches against both the Seller and the Company.
- Confirm there are no share mortgages, including any Riverlark security over the shares.
- Confirm there are no options, convertibles or other rights to issue shares.
- Completion deliverables: share certificates, signed transfers, and releases of any encumbrances.
- Uncapped title warranty (see item 2).

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
**Issue:** The Seller states that neither requires consent to a share sale. This is the Seller's own characterisation.

**Push back:**
- Our counsel should review both clauses independently. Lease provisions often deem a change of control to be an assignment.
- If there is any doubt, require landlord and Mossvale confirmation or waiver before Completion.
- At minimum, the Seller should give a warranty that no consent is required, backed by an indemnity.

### 15. Non-admission reservation (DL 1.4) and staleness
- DL 1.4 is acceptable as a non-admission clause. However, it must not be used to argue that a disclosure was "fair" when it hides the significance of a matter.
- The 22 September cut-off is about six weeks old. Require updated disclosure as at signing, and repetition of the warranties at Completion with no deemed disclosure against them.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Priority | Recommended Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Limitations apply to all Claims | High | Reverse the default. Carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, indemnities and leakage. Limit non-reliance |
| 2 | Title/capacity capped like general warranties | High | 100% cap, no thresholds, at least 6-year time limit |
| 3 | Cap / de minimis / basket / time | Medium | 30–50% cap (or W&I), AUD 10–15k de minimis, about AUD 120k tipping basket, 24 months |
| 4 | General data room disclosure | High | Specific, fair disclosure only. Updated Disclosure Letter at signing |
| 5 | Buyer knowledge exclusion | High | Delete, or limit to actual knowledge of named individuals |
| 6 | Tax / IP under general regime | High | Separate tax indemnity outside the limits. IP ownership treated as quasi-fundamental |
| 7 | Bluefen (30% of revenue) | Critical | Buyer-only-waivable Condition Precedent: unconditional consent plus clause 11.3 satisfied. Walk-right or escrow |
| 8 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Critical | Payoff and full release at Completion, paid from the price, change-of-control waiver |
| 9 | Bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs | High | Deduct as Transaction Costs/Debt, paid via payroll, indemnity, corrected funds flow |
| 10 | Ironquay SOW3 IP | High | Payment proof and confirmatory assignment as a Condition Precedent. Full-loss indemnity outside the limits |
| 11 | DD-006 privacy incident | High | Investigation report and NDB assessment before signing. Remediation covenant. Specific indemnity |
| 12 | Sandbar renewals AUD 330k | Medium | Obtain contracts. Aggregate for consent thresholds. Terminate, treat as Debt, or indemnify |
| 13 | Title via share register | High | ASIC/PPSR searches, encumbrance releases, uncapped title warranty |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | Medium | Independent review. Third-party confirmations if any doubt |
| 15 | Stale cut-off date | Medium | Updated disclosure at signing. Warranties repeated at Completion |

**Negotiation framing:** Lead with the inconsistencies between the Seller Update and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, items 7–12. Those inconsistencies are hard for the Seller to defend. Use them to justify the Conditions Precedent, specific indemnities and price deductions. Then trade on the general limitation numbers in item 3, which is where we have room to concede. Hold firm on items 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8.

Next steps: I can turn this into an issues list or a mark-up of the Seller Update. Before finalising, we should confirm these points against the full SPA draft and the DD-002 to DD-012 source documents.
=== END ADVICE ===
